name: How much does a rear-house addition cost in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: What is the realistic total cost of a rear addition in Los Angeles, including design, permits, construction, and city fees?
mainEntity.text: What is the realistic total cost of a rear addition in Los Angeles, including design, permits, construction, and city fees?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rear-house addition budget should be built from the total project cost, not just the construction bid. In Los Angeles-area cities, the final number is driven by square footage, whether the addition is one or two stories, how much structural work is needed, and the finish level. Design and engineering can be a meaningful part of the budget, especially if the existing home needs foundation upgrades, seismic reinforcement, or utility relocation. Permitting and plan check fees are another layer, and they can rise when the project is more complex or requires multiple review cycles. Homeowners should also reserve contingency funds because older homes often reveal hidden issues once demolition begins. The most useful budgeting approach is to separate soft costs, hard costs, city fees, and contingency so there are no surprises. A rear addition with luxury finishes and structural changes can cost far more than a straightforward room extension, so early scope control is essential.
acceptedAnswer.description: Costs vary widely based on size, finishes, structure, and permits, but rear additions in Los Angeles often run significantly higher than simpler interior remodels. The total budget should include design, engineering, plan check, permits, utility work, and construction contingency, not just framing and finishes.
